Strong at prioritising and managing multiple moving pieces
Sound judgement and know when to move quickly, when to escalate, and when to solve independently
Comfortable improving processes and building structure
Detail-oriented, but also focused on the bigger picture

Active use of generative AI tools to enhance efficiency

Collaborate with different IT teams to support multi-platforms’ integration and risk data generation effort.

Renewal Pricing and Retention Strategy
Persistency and Customer Retention Analytics
Actuarial Pricing and Product Management
Portfolio Profitability Management
Price Elasticity Modeling

Predictive Modeling, AI, and Decision Optimization
Insurance Data and Analytics

Identifies and implements enhancements to billing workflows, controls, and reporting mechanisms

Collaborates across departments to improve financial processes, strengthen controls, and ensure alignment with institutional objectives

jobs.description:

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity

eDiscovery Services within Forensics operates as a managed service, combining internal operational delivery with client-facing consulting support. At the Senior level, professionals serve as experienced contributors within this model, executing and coordinating end-to-end Discovery activities, including legal hold, evidence management, data processing, review support and production, across complex investigations, litigation and consulting matters.

You will apply sound judgment and technical expertise to help ensure work is performed accurately, defensibly and in alignment with EY standards. You will play a key role in maintaining quality, supporting analysts and escalating issues as needed while contributing to services for flagship clients and high-profile matters.

You will advise clients on data-driven solutions to forensic issues and matters involving business conduct and ethics. Working with clients and Forensic Data Analytics teams, you will help design and implement assets that identify risks of non-compliance and deliver insights from data. You will also analyze large volumes of data to identify high-risk relationships and actions related to fraud, bribery and corruption, ethics and other regulatory risks.

Your key responsibilities

Lead and oversee Discovery activities in accordance with established methodologies, engagement requirements and EY standards.
Ensure defensible chain of custody and documentation by supervising data preparation for review and validating that final deliverables meet defined quality, compliance and engagement specifications.
Proactively identify, assess and drive resolution of processing or quality issues by applying standard protocols, reviewing quality control outputs and directing remediation efforts.
Provide day-to-day guidance and on-the-job support to junior team members, contribute to training efforts, and maintain and enhance internal documentation and playbooks as procedures and data sources evolve.
Supervise junior staff and provide direction and oversight regarding their activities.
Contribute to one or more processes, solutions or projects by completing agreed activities, applying judgment and selecting appropriate methodologies to inform recommendations while considering success criteria, barriers, risks and issues.
Meet individual targets that affect the immediate team and locally established performance objectives related to client service, quality and risk management, solution development and teaming.
Apply analytical judgment, approved methodologies and technology to evaluate complex electronic data, prioritize issues and make sound decisions that support engagement objectives.
Exercise judgment and discretion when supervising junior staff and escalate risk appropriately.
Take responsibility for the high-quality execution and delivery of assigned parts of Discovery engagements and help oversee multiple projects to confirm that work meets client needs and EY quality standards.
Use technology to provide deliverables, continue learning and share knowledge with other team members.
Develop relationships with professionals in other service lines and seek opportunities to work together.
Balance multiple concurrent projects, competing priorities and deadlines, and delegate workload to colleagues or staff as needed.
Develop others by seeking and offering on-the-job coaching and feedback.
Apply strong written and oral communication skills and careful attention to detail when managing the quality of services provided by the Discovery operations team.

To qualify for the role you must have

A bachelor’s degree in business, technology entrepreneurship, computer science, informatics, statistics, applied mathematics, data science or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience
A minimum of two years of Discovery experience
Strong knowledge of the Discovery lifecycle, its components and tools such as SQL, Relativity, EnCase or other Discovery tools
Excellent project and time management skills, including the ability to prioritize work across multiple engagements
A proven record of delivering Discovery solutions to large, complex organizations
The ability and willingness to travel and work in excess of standard hours when necessary
Access to reliable transportation to and from the EY office and client sites. A driver’s license is strongly recommended because ride-share and public transportation options may not be available in all locations

Ideally, you’ll also have

An active professional designation, or progress toward one, such as CFE, CFCE, RCA or EnCE

What we look for

We look for experienced professionals who combine technical Discovery knowledge with sound judgment, careful execution and practical team leadership. You should be comfortable overseeing complex work, directing junior colleagues, escalating risks, managing competing priorities and maintaining high standards for defensibility, client service and quality.

What We Offer You

At EY, we harness our collective strength to empower you to shape your future with confidence through professional growth, personal fulfillment and an inclusive culture. Learn more at ey.com/us/careers.

We offer a comprehensive compensation and benefits package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to the business. The base salary range for this job is:

New York City, Boston, and Washington DC Metro Areas, Washington State, and Southern California offices – $109,000 to $163,600
Bay Area California offices – $113,500 to $170,400
All other offices locations in the US, including Sacramento – $90,800 to $149,900

Individual salaries within these ranges are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge, skills and geography. In addition, our Total Rewards package includes medical and dental coverage, pension and 401(k) plans, and a wide range of paid time off options.
Under our flexible vacation policy, you’ll decide how much vacation time you need based on your own personal circumstances. You’ll also be granted time off for designated EY Paid Holidays, Winter/Summer breaks, Personal/Family Care, and other leaves of absence when needed to support your physical, financial, and emotional well-being.

Are you ready to shape your future with confidence? Apply today.

To make the most of your application experience, please limit yourself to two applications within a six-month period.
EY accepts applications for this position on an on-going basis.

Enabled by data, AI and advanced technology, EY teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow.

jobs.title: Manager, Global Consumer Insights & Research
jobs.description:
The NFL's Marketing Strategy, Planning & Insights team serves as a center of excellence for the League, shaping how the NFL grows fans, strengthens the brand, and drives engagement across the U.S. and international markets. The team brings together consumer insights, audience strategy, business planning, initiative-level strategy, and performance measurement to ground decisions in fan understanding, market dynamics, and business priorities. Partnering across business functions and key stakeholders (e.g., the 32 NFL Clubs, partners), the team delivers actionable insights, strategic guidance, and planning frameworks that inform both long-term strategy and day-to-day decisions.

Within this team, Consumer Insights designs and conducts primary research, integrates syndicated and first-party data, and delivers actionable insights across global fan development, brand health, media, live events, marketing effectiveness, partnerships, social responsibility, and player-related priorities.

The Manager, Global Strategic Insights supports research development, analysis, and insights generation to inform global fan development and business growth. The role conducts and synthesizes primary research, syndicated sources, first-party data, and market intelligence to ensure Leaguewide decision-making is grounded in a fan-first perspective.

Responsibilities

Global Fandom Intelligence

Monitor fandom, avidity, engagement, and brand health, as well as the drivers of and barriers to each.
Analyze cultural, behavioral, and regional differences to identify opportunities to acquire, develop, engage, and monetize fans.
Leverage NFL-specific and macro landscape insights to support the development of audience-level strategies by demographic, market, and other relevant segmentation lenses, such as engagement level and football knowledge.

Strategic Insights & Business Planning

Support strategic analyses, forecasts, scenario planning, and performance measurement tied to near- and long-range priorities.
Connect fan behavior, research findings, and marketplace trends to business opportunities and actionable recommendations.
Develop executive-ready presentations, memos, and key planning documents.

Consumer Insights & Research Execution

Support qualitative and quantitative research from objective setting and methodology selection through questionnaire or discussion guide development, analysis, and reporting.
Manage day-to-day stakeholder and vendor coordination, timelines, and deliverables across multiple projects.
Synthesize primary research, syndicated data, first-party information, and secondary sources into concise, story-driven visuals and recommendations using best-in-class practices.

Brand, Media & Marketing Effectiveness

Measure brand campaigns, creative effectiveness, audience sentiment, cultural relevance, and other equity measures across markets and fan segments.
Analyze broadcast, streaming, direct-to-consumer, content, and emerging viewing experiences to inform audience growth, media, product, and marketing strategies.
Evaluate new products, events, experiences, and fan engagement initiatives across the NFL ecosystem.

Stakeholder Partnership & Team Contribution

Build collaborative relationships across the League, Clubs, markets, and external research partners, advocating for fan-centric, insight-driven decisions.
Communicate complex research through clear, concise storytelling tailored to varied audiences.
Coordinate multiple workstreams while maintaining quality, timing, and business relevance.
Support junior team members through coaching and project guidance, and improve research processes, reporting standards, and insight socialization.

Required Qualifications

5+ years of relevant experience in consumer insights, market research, strategy, analytics, or a related field.
Ability to translate business questions into research objectives and quantitative or qualitative research plans.
Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex findings and communicate concise, actionable insights to varied stakeholders.
Strong data visualization and storytelling skills, with experience creating executive-ready presentations and insight-driven reports.
Strong project management, cross-functional collaboration, and relationship-building skills in a fast-paced environment.
Experience with research methods such as segmentation, surveys, ethnography, interviews, and focus groups, plus familiarity with syndicated media measurement and applied analytics.
Proficiency with analytical tools such as Microsoft Excel, SPSS, or Q.
Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline or equivalent professional experience.

Other Key Attributes / Characteristics

Experience managing vendors and/or analysts; strong people management capabilities preferred.
Familiarity with sports and entertainment; knowledge of media and live events is a plus.
Experience working with global or multinational businesses and measurement frameworks strongly preferred.
Spanish, Portuguese, French, and/or German language proficiency is a plus.
Master’s degree in Market Research preferred.

Terms / Expected Hours of Work

Some travel required
NFL employees are required to work in office

Salary / Pay Range

Job Summary: We are seeking an Associate to support and drive automation initiatives within our Wealth Management Operations division. You will work closely with operations teams to identify high-impact process automation opportunities and implement solutions using RPA platforms (such as UiPath, Power Automate, etc..) and scripting languages (Python, VBA, SQL, etc.). • Process Analysis & Opportunity Identification: Work with TEMCO teams to uncover automation use cases, evaluate feasibility and potential value, and prioritize quick-win opportunities. Clearly document business requirements, acceptance criteria, and expected outcomes for each initiative.

*** HM: "Consulting experience is a plus however the role is primarily an automation and data analytics position. We are looking for someone with advanced technical background in building automation solutions. "

1. Minimum 5 years' experience

Strong scripting/programming skills in languages like Python, VBA, or SQL for building custom automation scripts and integrations.
• Domain Knowledge: Solid understanding of Wealth Management Operations processes, including areas like trade processing, settlements, reconciliations, client reporting, reference data, and exception management.
• Analytical & Problem-Solving Skills: Demonstrated strength in business analysis, process mapping, and problem-solving. Ability to analyze complex operational workflows, identify inefficiencies, and define improvement solutions. Critical thinking skills to challenge assumptions, validate automation outcomes, and ensure solutions are robust and error proofed by design.

Bachelor's Degree

Experience partnering with multiple stakeholders in a fast driven environment.

jobs.title: Financial Planning Analyst
jobs.description:
Advisors · RIAs · Portfolio Workflows

About the job

PortfolioFuture is an independent fund discovery and intelligence company. We use empirical research to discover, evaluate, and rank ETFs and mutual funds, and identify where they can credibly compete for allocations in portfolios.

Our research connects more than 10,000 funds with institutional investors, 23,000+ advisory firms, and 400,000+ financial advisors, supporting fund discovery, portfolio analytics, and asset-manager distribution intelligence.

As a Financial Planning Analyst, you will study how financial advisors and wealth managers evaluate the funds PortfolioFuture identifies. The role covers advisor research, portfolio workflows, fund consideration, and the development of market intelligence used across PortfolioFuture.

You will speak with advisors, RIAs, and wealth-management professionals to understand what makes a fund worth investigating, what keeps it out of a portfolio, and how those judgments differ across firms and client types.

What you’ll work on

• Speak with financial advisors, RIAs, and wealth-management professionals about funds identified through PortfolioFuture’s research.
• Study how advisors compare competing ETFs and mutual funds and what makes a fund worth further consideration.
• Document the recurring questions, objections, and concerns that come up around specific funds and investment strategies.
• Research how advisors judge a fund’s strategy, positioning, fees, track record, and role in a portfolio.
• Compare how different advisors evaluate the same investment product.
• Turn qualitative conversations into structured market intelligence the rest of PortfolioFuture can act on.
• Identify gaps between how a fund manager describes a strategy and how the wealth-management market understands it.
• Study how a fund enters an advisor’s consideration set and what moves it from awareness to real due diligence.
• Work with PortfolioFuture’s substitution and decomposition research so advisor conversations stay grounded in evidence.
• Use large language models and other tools to organize, summarize, and analyze qualitative research at scale.
• Share what you learn with research, product, and distribution teams so findings reach the people who can use them.
• Test whether the patterns you observe hold across firm size, client type, and market environment.

What we’re looking for

• Background in finance, economics, business, wealth management, communications, or a related field.
• Strong interest in financial advisors, RIAs, wealth management, ETFs, and mutual funds.
• Ability to conduct thoughtful professional conversations and ask useful follow-up questions.
• Ability to understand an investment product well enough to discuss it with experienced advisors.
• Strong listening skills and the ability to identify patterns across many different conversations.
• Ability to turn qualitative feedback into clear, structured written findings.
• Comfort reaching out to and speaking with experienced wealth-management professionals.
• Ability to communicate what you learned clearly, including what you are not yet sure about.
• Experience in wealth management, financial advisory, investment product distribution, or practice management is useful but not required.
• Experience with research interviews, qualitative analysis, CRM data, or survey design is a plus.

PortfolioFuture research

Fund Substitution identifies ETFs and mutual funds that can serve similar portfolio roles, using return similarity, relative performance, tracking error, and fees.

Fund Decomposition separates returns explained by investable market exposures from residual performance, evaluating replication quality, residual alpha, and risk.

Fund Opportunity ranks ETFs and mutual funds across four dimensions: Similar Fund Ranking, Addressable Market, Pure Alpha, and Diversification Benefits.

PortfolioFuture’s research is independent. Commercial relationships do not affect which funds are surfaced, how they rank, or the conclusions reached.

**Position Overview**

We are seeking a highly motivated **Financial Analyst** to join our Finance team. The Financial Analyst will play a key role in supporting financial planning, cash flow analysis, working capital management, and management reporting activities across the organization.

* Analyze trends in Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, and Inventory balances.

* Support monthly financial reviews and variance analysis.

**Reporting & Business Analysis**

* Prepare recurring management reports, dashboards, and KPI analyses.
* Support monthly close activities through financial analysis and reporting.
* Identify trends, risks, and opportunities impacting business performance.
* Assist in ad-hoc financial analyses and special projects as assigned.
* Support the preparation of presentations for senior leadership.

**Process Improvement**

* Assist in improving financial reporting processes and analytical capabilities.
* Contribute to automation initiatives within Microsoft Dynamics 365 and reporting platforms.
* Recommend improvements to reporting accuracy, efficiency, and data quality.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field.

* Strong proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including advanced formulas, pivot tables, and financial modeling.
* Experience analyzing financial statements, cash flow, and operational metrics.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
* Excellent communication and presentation skills.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 or similar ERP systems.

The successful candidate will be evaluated on:

* Accuracy and reliability of cash flow forecasting.

**JOB DESCRIPTION**  
  
  

Morgan Health is a mission-driven healthcare organization within JPMorgan Chase focused on improving the quality, affordability, and experience of employer-sponsored healthcare. We operate with the focus and agility of a smaller, specialized team, backed by the scale, resources, and reach of one of the world's largest companies. Our team brings together healthcare, data, research, investment, and policy expertise to tackle some of the most complex challenges facing employers and their employees. If you are someone who wants their technical work to have a tangible impact on healthcare, this is a unique opportunity to build within a highly collaborative team to further Morgan Health's mission.

As a Senior Analytics Engineer within Morgan Health, you'll play a key role in building the data foundation behind that work. You'll have meaningful ownership of Morgan Health's analytics environment, partnering closely with data scientists as well as other internal and external stakeholders to turn complex healthcare data into trusted, production-ready data marts that support research, insights, and decision-making. In this role, you will have the opportunity to shape how analytics engineering is done within Morgan Health — not simply inherit an established process. You will own and evolve core elements of the analytics life cycle, from data modeling and testing to CI/CD, monitoring and quality standards. Because we're a focused team, you will work closely with the people using the data and have visibility into how your work contributes to healthcare research, insights, and ultimately better outcomes.

**This role is in-office five days per week, based in either New York, NY or Washington, DC.**

* Develop and maintain Morgan Health's healthcare data models (e.g., marts and curated datasets) using SQL and dbt
* Create proof of concept (POC) solutions of data products per data scientist design requirements; iterate rapidly to refine requirements and evolve POCs to production-level solutions
* Design and evolve a robust automated testing framework (e.g., dbt tests, custom checks, risk-based testing strategies)

* Demonstrated ownership of the full lifecycle of a dbt project, including automated testing, CI/CD and deployment, environment/version management, monitoring, and ongoing performance and reliability of the analytics layer in production
* Hands-on experience using Databricks (or similar platforms) to develop, deploy, and support data pipelines and analytics workflows in a production environment; experience working with Python or R for analysis, testing, and automation
* Proven track record of creating and maintaining data models, data marts, and transformations that support multiple competing analytical use cases
* Strong written and verbal communication skills with an ability to effectively interface within cross-functional teams (data scientists, analytics engineering, product/architecture, and platform partners)

**Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills**

* Experience working with health care data (e.g., medical and pharmaceutical claims, eligibility, provider, survey, or biometrics data), common medical groupers, and quality measurement standards
* Advanced degree in a quantitative field such as computer science, information systems, engineering, or a related discipline
* Experience using AI-assisted coding tools to develop, test, and improve SQL, Python, and analytics engineering workflows
* Experience supporting analytics platforms in regulated and/or privacy-sensitive environments
* Demonstrated ability to successfully multitask, balance competing priorities, and deliver high-quality work in a fast-paced environment

jobs.description:
Heart to Heart is seeking a Business Technology Analyst to help improve, support, and expand the technology our teams use every day.

You will work directly with teams across the organization to understand how they operate, identify opportunities for improvement, and help turn those needs into practical technology solutions.

The role is well suited for an early-career professional who is technically curious, learns quickly, and enjoys solving problems. The work will include system configuration, automation, troubleshooting, process improvement, user support, and participation in new technology initiatives, including the growing use of AI across the organization.

* Bachelor's degree in a related technical field

* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills

* Ability to learn new software and systems quickly

* Strong attention to detail

* Interest in automation, AI, and emerging technologies

* Able to work onsite in East Orange, New Jersey five days per week

Experience or familiarity with one or more of the following is helpful, but not required:

* Airtable or similar low-code platforms

* Microsoft 365

* Power Automate, Zapier, Make, or similar automation tools

* Excel or Google Sheets

* Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, or other AI tools

* Relational database concepts

* APIs or basic scripting

* Process mapping and documentation

* Healthcare, nonprofit, or intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) environments

**Responsibilities**

* Build, maintain, and improve solutions using Airtable, Microsoft 365, and other business platforms

* Create automations and integrations that reduce manual work and improve efficiency

* Work with business teams to understand requirements and translate them into practical technology solutions

* Support technology improvement projects, including process automation and the use of AI in everyday operations

* Troubleshoot issues and provide day-to-day technology support to staff

jobs.title: Wealth Research Analyst
jobs.description:
Advisors · RIAs · Portfolio Workflows

About the job

PortfolioFuture is an independent fund discovery and intelligence company. We use empirical research to discover, evaluate, and rank ETFs and mutual funds, and identify where they can credibly compete for allocations in portfolios.

Our research connects more than 10,000 funds with institutional investors, 23,000+ advisory firms, and 400,000+ financial advisors, supporting fund discovery, portfolio analytics, and asset-manager distribution intelligence.

As a Wealth Research Analyst, you will study how financial advisors and wealth managers evaluate the funds PortfolioFuture identifies. The role covers advisor research, portfolio workflows, fund consideration, and the development of market intelligence used across PortfolioFuture.

You will speak with advisors, RIAs, and wealth-management professionals to understand what makes a fund worth investigating, what keeps it out of a portfolio, and how those judgments differ across firms and client types.

What you’ll work on

• Speak with financial advisors, RIAs, and wealth-management professionals about funds identified through PortfolioFuture’s research.
• Study how advisors compare competing ETFs and mutual funds and what makes a fund worth further consideration.
• Document the recurring questions, objections, and concerns that come up around specific funds and investment strategies.
• Research how advisors judge a fund’s strategy, positioning, fees, track record, and role in a portfolio.
• Compare how different advisors evaluate the same investment product.
• Turn qualitative conversations into structured market intelligence the rest of PortfolioFuture can act on.
• Identify gaps between how a fund manager describes a strategy and how the wealth-management market understands it.
• Study how a fund enters an advisor’s consideration set and what moves it from awareness to real due diligence.
• Work with PortfolioFuture’s substitution and decomposition research so advisor conversations stay grounded in evidence.
• Use large language models and other tools to organize, summarize, and analyze qualitative research at scale.
• Share what you learn with research, product, and distribution teams so findings reach the people who can use them.
• Test whether the patterns you observe hold across firm size, client type, and market environment.

What we’re looking for

• Background in finance, economics, business, wealth management, communications, or a related field.
• Strong interest in financial advisors, RIAs, wealth management, ETFs, and mutual funds.
• Ability to conduct thoughtful professional conversations and ask useful follow-up questions.
• Ability to understand an investment product well enough to discuss it with experienced advisors.
• Strong listening skills and the ability to identify patterns across many different conversations.
• Ability to turn qualitative feedback into clear, structured written findings.
• Comfort reaching out to and speaking with experienced wealth-management professionals.
• Ability to communicate what you learned clearly, including what you are not yet sure about.
• Experience in wealth management, financial advisory, investment product distribution, or practice management is useful but not required.
• Experience with research interviews, qualitative analysis, CRM data, or survey design is a plus.

PortfolioFuture research

Fund Substitution identifies ETFs and mutual funds that can serve similar portfolio roles, using return similarity, relative performance, tracking error, and fees.

Fund Decomposition separates returns explained by investable market exposures from residual performance, evaluating replication quality, residual alpha, and risk.

Fund Opportunity ranks ETFs and mutual funds across four dimensions: Similar Fund Ranking, Addressable Market, Pure Alpha, and Diversification Benefits.

PortfolioFuture’s research is independent. Commercial relationships do not affect which funds are surfaced, how they rank, or the conclusions reached.

jobs.title: Junior Compliance Analyst
jobs.description:
About Pockyt

Pockyt is building the AI-native infrastructure for global money movement. We give merchants a single platform to accept payments from anywhere, send money globally, and manage funds through Global Virtual Accounts and stablecoins — but our ambition runs deeper than the rails themselves. We're architecting the connective tissue that lets capital move across borders the way information moves across the internet: instantly, intelligently, and autonomously.
We serve a wide spectrum of merchants, from sophisticated enterprise platforms running complex multi-currency operations to the next generation of AI-powered startups, including the one-person unicorns we believe are about to reshape the global economy. Today, that means one integration, one account view, and one place to track everything. Tomorrow, it means a financial layer that AI agents can natively transact on — where money flows are orchestrated, optimized, and reconciled without human bottlenecks.

Our mission is to make global commerce frictionless. We're not building another payments platform. We're building the operating system for how value moves in an agentic, borderless economy.

The Role

We're hiring a Junior Compliance Analyst to keep the engine of our compliance function running. You'll own the high-volume, detail-heavy work that every good compliance program depends on across both our cross-border payments and merchant acquiring programs: chasing documents, checking files for completeness, clearing first-level screening hits, prepping evidence packages, and keeping case records clean and audit-ready. When something needs a judgment call, you'll assemble the facts and escalate it to the Compliance Manager or CCO with a clear summary — and you'll learn how those calls get made.

This is a great fit for someone early in their compliance career who is meticulous, likes a well-organized queue, and wants a fast, hands-on education in BSA/AML and merchant acquiring compliance at a cross-border payments company. Because we're actively automating our workflows with our Product Engineering team, you'll also be the person who knows exactly where the repetitive work lives — and your notes on it will shape what gets automated next.

What You'll Do

Onboarding file prep:
Collect and chase merchant KYB/KYC documents, check applications for completeness, verify basic entity and UBO details against registries, and flag gaps before a file goes to review
Merchant acquiring support:
Help underwrite new card-acquiring merchants by verifying business model and MCC, reviewing merchant websites for prohibited or restricted products and required policies (refunds, terms, privacy), and checking principals against MATCH and internal decline lists; escalate anything outside our risk appetite with a clear summary
First-level screening:
Run and clear obvious false-positive sanctions, PEP, and adverse media hits; document the rationale; escalate anything ambiguous with a clean summary
L1 transaction monitoring triage:
Work through ThetaRay alerts (in transition to a new tool), close out clear-cut false positives per the playbook, and route the rest up with the relevant transaction history pulled together
Acquiring risk monitoring:
Track merchant chargeback and fraud ratios against card network thresholds, flag merchants trending toward program limits, and pull the transaction and dispute data the Compliance Manager needs to decide next steps
RFI coordination:
Draft and send routine RFIs to merchants, track responses and deadlines, follow up on overdue items, and log what comes back
Periodic review support:
Pull refreshed documents, re-run screening, and assemble the review file so the Compliance Manager can make the call
Evidence and record-keeping:
Maintain case logs, organize evidence packages in SharePoint, and keep trackers accurate so any file can be handed to a banking partner or examiner on short notice
Data pulls and reporting:
Pull alert, case, onboarding, and chargeback metrics for weekly reviews, quarterly QA, and banking- and acquiring-partner requests
Process notes:
Keep a running list of repetitive steps and friction points, and help test AI-assisted and automated versions of your workflows once they ship

What We're Looking For

0–2 years in compliance, risk, KYC/onboarding, fraud operations, or a related role at a fintech, MSB, bank, or payments company — or a relevant internship plus strong interest in financial crimes
Exceptional attention to detail — you notice the mismatched date of birth, the expired document, and the missing page
Comfort with high-volume, repetitive work and the discipline to do it accurately every time
Strong organization — you can manage a queue, track deadlines, and keep a clean paper trail without being reminded
Good judgment about when to escalate, and the ability to summarize a case clearly and briefly
Clear, professional written communication with merchants and internal teams
AI fluency, or eagerness to build it — you're comfortable using Claude (or similar) for document review, summarization, and drafting
Curiosity about cross-border payments, stablecoins, and how compliance works in practice

Bonus Points

CAMS (or working toward it), ACAMS membership, or comparable training
Exposure to sanctions screening or transaction monitoring tools (ThetaRay, Hummingbird, Unit21, ComplyAdvantage, or similar)
Experience with KYB document review for business entities, especially cross-border or multi-entity structures
Exposure to merchant underwriting, card acquiring, or payment facilitator (PayFac) onboarding, including familiarity with Visa/Mastercard network rules, MCCs, MATCH, or chargeback/fraud monitoring programs such as Visa VAMP or Mastercard ECM/EFM
Mandarin, Spanish, or Portuguese language skills (helpful for LATAM/APAC merchant documents)
Strong spreadsheet skills for tracking and data pulls

How You'll Work

Rhythm:
Work the daily queue → clear or escalate → document → keep trackers current; weekly case reviews with the team and CCO; regular check-ins with the Compliance Manager on escalations
Collaboration:
Daily with onboarding and the Compliance Manager; regular contact with merchants on RFIs and document requests; occasional handoffs to product engineering on workflow fixes
Quality bar:
Every file you touch is complete and organized; every cleared hit has a documented rationale; every escalation arrives with the facts already pulled together

Success looks like:
a queue that stays current, onboarding files that reach review complete the first time, clean and consistent case records, fast RFI turnaround, early flags on merchants trending toward chargeback limits, and a growing ability to handle more of the decision-making yourself.

Why Pockyt

Learn compliance from the ground up at a fast-moving, AI-native fintech, working directly alongside the CCO and Compliance Manager
Real exposure to onboarding, merchant acquiring, sanctions, transaction monitoring, and banking-partner work from day one
A clear growth path to Compliance Analyst and Senior Compliance Analyst as your judgment and scope grow
Competitive compensation, employer-paid health insurance, 401(k) match, and unlimited PTO
Quarterly bonus pay-outs
of up to 20% of your base salary

Company Description

Etsy is the global marketplace for unique and creative goods. We build, power, and evolve the tools and technologies that connect millions of entrepreneurs with millions of buyers around the world. As an Etsy employee, you will tackle unique, meaningful, and large-scale problems alongside passionate coworkers, all the while making a rewarding impact and Keeping Commerce Human.

That means hiring great people, setting them up for success from day one, and giving them real reasons to grow their careers here. We invest in development that goes beyond promotions, and we foster the trust and relationships that help people do their best work together.

What’s the role?

We are looking for a Market Researcher who can influence marketing decision-making by deeply understanding Etsy’s audiences and our evolving competitive landscape. You’ll work closely with marketing teams and alongside other researchers and data scientists to deliver insights and recommendations that will craft the future of human commerce on Etsy.

This is a full-time position reporting to the Senior Manager, Market Research.

What’s this team like at Etsy?

The Market Research team helps Etsy understand customers, sellers, and the marketplace through rigorous qualitative and quantitative research
We use research to inform the development of marketing strategy & tactics and to help evaluate marketing performance (in close partnership with Marketing Analytics)
We’re a mixed-methods team with a deep bench of quantitative and qualitative methods, but our team leans towards quantitative skill sets
We conduct research with global consumers, small business owners, as well as Etsy buyers & sellers
We actively foster an inclusive team culture that promotes diversity, collaboration, and professional development

What does the day-to-day look like?

Primary Tasks:
Partners with Product & Retention Marketing teams to guide marketing strategy and execution
Independently develop and execute research for tightly-scoped research projects, including developing survey instruments, analyzing data, generating insights and recommendations, and writing reports, while supporting the Product & Retention Marketing Research Lead on more widely-scoped research projects

Secondary Tasks:
Own key aspects of our brand tracking program, including vendor relationships, questionnaire updates, tabulation specs, data analysis, and reporting
Source and synthesize secondary research, including competitive intelligence
Contribute to market research operations, including project management and overseeing the process of working with third-party research vendors (e.g., research agencies, moderators)
Of course, this is just a sample of the kinds of work this role will require! You should assume that your role will encompass other tasks, too, and that your job duties and responsibilities may change from time to time at Etsy's discretion, or otherwise applicable with local law.

Qualities that will help you thrive in this role are:

Approximately 3+ years experience conducting primary market research, including brand tracking experience
Familiarity with lifecycle marketing and the ability to translate research into concrete marketing recommendations
Strong quantitative research skills, including sampling, questionnaire design, data analysis (including strong understanding of statistical testing), and reporting
Experience conducting research that shapes lifecycle marketing strategy
Experience conducting product marketing research– such as positioning development, GTM message testing, or value prop testing
Comfort leveraging AI tools to accelerate research workflows while maintaining human oversight and judgement of outputs
Excellent data visualization skills, including experience with Google Slides, with the ability to translate complex data into clear narratives
Strong communication skills
A collaborative, curious, and pragmatic mindset and the ability to balance methodological rigor with speed

Compensation & Benefits

In addition to salary, you'll be eligible for an equity package, an annual performance bonus, and our competitive benefits that support you and your family. Base salary is determined by your location, skills, and experience.

Etsy uses two geographic pay zones to reflect the labor markets where we compete for talent: one called Geo-1, covering the New York City metropolitan area, San Francisco Bay Area, and Seattle metropolitan area, and one called Geo-2, covering all other U.S. locations. We prioritize candidates based within commutable distance of Etsy’s Brooklyn Office. Depending on proximity, we ask team members to come in once or twice per week. Remote candidates outside commutable distance may be considered on a case-by-case basis, with the expectation of occasional travel to the office. Learn more details about our work modes and workplace safety policies here.

**Location(s):** Step Up Family Services is seeking Board Certified Behavior Analysts (BCBAs) for current and future opportunities throughout **Southern** **New Jersey.**

**Service Areas:** Camden, Burlington, Gloucester, Atlantic, Cumberland, Salem, and Cape May counties, including communities such as Cherry Hill, Voorhees, Mount Laurel, Washington Township, Vineland, Egg Harbor Township, and surrounding areas.

We provide individualized, high-quality behavioral health services that build on individual strengths and create lasting progress in the communities we serve.

Our Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) services support children and families through evidence-based interventions delivered in home, center-based, and community settings. We are seeking dedicated BCBA/LBA professionals who are passionate about clinical excellence, developing Behavior Technicians, and helping children achieve meaningful outcomes.

* **Supportive Team:** Collaborative clinical and operational support so you can focus on delivering high-quality care.

**Position Summary**: The **BCBA/LBA** provides clinical leadership and oversight of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) services for children and families served by Step Up Family Services. This role is responsible for conducting assessments, developing and monitoring individualized treatment and Behavior Support Plans (BSPs), analyzing client progress, supervising and developing BTs/RBTs, and partnering with families to support meaningful and sustainable outcomes.

The BCBA/LBA is expected to exercise independent clinical decision-making while maintaining high standards of ethical practice, documentation, collaboration, and regulatory compliance.

* Provide ongoing supervision, observation, coaching, and clinical direction to BTs/RBTs, ensuring treatment fidelity, staff competency, and appropriate implementation of treatment protocols.
* Partner with parents and caregivers through education, training, modeling, and ongoing communication to promote treatment consistency and generalization of skills across environments.
* Collaborate with families, BTs/RBTs, clinical leadership, schools, providers, and other members of the care team to support coordinated and clinically appropriate care.
* Maintain ownership of assigned caseloads, including authorized service hours, supervision requirements, scheduling, reassessments, treatment-plan updates, and required clinical documentation.
* Identify and appropriately respond to clinical, ethical, safety, or professional-boundary concerns, including consultation and escalation when necessary.
* Complete all clinical documentation, assessments, treatment plans, supervision records, and other required records accurately and within established timeframes, utilizing Step Up’s required electronic systems.
* Maintain compliance with BACB ethical requirements, New Jersey licensure requirements, payer/funding requirements, Step Up policies, and all applicable professional and regulatory standards.

**Qualifications**

* Master’s degree or higher in Applied Behavior Analysis, Psychology, Education, or another qualifying related field.
* Demonstrated experience providing ABA services and developing individualized behavioral treatment interventions.
* Experience conducting FBAs, developing treatment/BSPs, analyzing clinical data, and modifying interventions based on client progress.
* Experience supervising, coaching, or developing BTs/RBTs or other direct-care clinical staff.
* Strong clinical decision-making, communication, organization, documentation, and interpersonal skills.
* Ability to work effectively and independently across in-home and/or center-based environments while maintaining strong collaboration with families and the broader clinical team.
* Reliable transportation and ability to travel to assigned client homes, community settings, or Step Up centers as required.

jobs.title: Revenue Operations Analyst
jobs.description:
The Revenue Operations Analyst supports the firm's corporate revenue programs and its enterprise technology and data agreements, working with program owners to maintain data, prepare reporting, track obligations, and coordinate follow-up. This role works across Sales, Operations, Growth, Accounting, FP&A, Legal, Marketing, and Technology.
  
  
The firm is scaling a set of corporate revenue programs, including strategic partnerships, qualified leads, and managed accounts, that generate revenue alongside the agent platform. It is also expanding a centralized model for the enterprise software and data agreements that support the field. Both require the same discipline: clean attribution, tracked obligations, recurring reporting, and a clear view of what the firm earns and what it spends. This role supports that discipline and prepares the reporting that shows what each program and agreement returns.  
  
The base salary range for this role is $115,000– $130,000 per year. This position is eligible for a discretionary performance-based bonus. The exact bonus is not guaranteed and will vary based on individual performance, team results, and company performance. Actual pay will be determined by factors such as education, experience, and job-related skills relevant to the role. Marcus & Millichap is a multi-state employer and posted salary ranges are provided in good faith for compliance with all relevant pay-transparency regulations. These ranges may not reflect potential compensation for positions based in other states or regions.

**Responsibilities**

**Revenue Program Operations.** Support the day-to-day operations across the firm's corporate revenue programs: strategic partnerships, qualified leads, and managed accounts. Working alongside each program's owner, maintain the operating flow and attribution model for each within the CRM, and help extend them as the programs evolve. Reconcile partner-reported figures against internal data and flag variances and amounts owed for resolution. Document program rules and standard operating procedures as they are agreed. Recommend changes to program design where the data warrants. Support partner relationship coverage as the portfolio scales.

**Revenue Tech Stack & Vendor Governance****.** Maintain a firmwide inventory of the platforms, data subscriptions, and productivity tools the sales organization runs on. Track contract terms, cost, license counts, and utilization for each, so renewal decisions are made on evidence. Run a central calendar of obligations, renewals, and notice periods spanning partner and vendor agreements. Provide the usage and cost analysis that informs subscription strategy and consolidation decisions, and support tool evaluation and renewal negotiations. Support day-to-day vendor communications for select tools, including reporting requests, escalation tracking, and renewal preparation.

**Agent Support Spend****.** Run the day-to-day process for agent support dollars: partner with Accounting on attribution, maintain the approval and provisioning workflow, and prepare reporting on utilization and cost allocation. Help shape how allocations are tracked as the program formalizes.

**Financial Attribution & Reporting****.** Prepare the recurring reporting that connects program and agreement performance to the firm's financials, covering attribution accuracy, referral conversion, managed account performance, and return on engagement. Apply consistent measurement standards from launch so programs can be compared as they scale. Partner with Accounting and FP&A so revenue earned and spend committed are attributed, invoiced, and recorded correctly, connecting program and vendor economics to the firm's P&L. Report on program impact for market, divisional, and finance leadership.

**The Person**

**Qualifications & Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in business, finance, economics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

* 3–4 years in business operations, revenue operations, vendor or contract management, financial planning and analysis, or a comparable analytical and operational role.

* Working knowledge of financial data, including cost, revenue, and budget reporting.

* Comfort working with data in Excel, a CRM (Salesforce preferred), and a business intelligence platform (Tableau preferred). Able to define requirements, validate what is built, and prepare reporting. Administrator-level expertise is not required.

* Track record of owning a recurring process with financial consequence, such as a close, a reconciliation, a renewal cycle, or a reporting package.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Familiarity with how a P&L is structured.

* Experience administering vendor contracts, renewals, or software licensing at scale.

* Experience supporting a workforce of independent contractors, franchisees, or other populations where program adoption depends on demonstrated value.

* Commercial real estate, professional services, or brokerage exposure.

* Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and comfort using AI tools within a daily workflow.

**Competencies & Characteristics**

* Comfortable where definitions, systems, and precedent are still being established.

* Strong written and verbal communication; effective with both technical and executive stakeholders.

* Identifies what needs to happen next and moves it forward.

* Follows a discrepancy to its source rather than working around it.

* Thinks critically about the work and brings solutions alongside the problems.

* Self-motivated, with high attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple and competing priorities.

jobs.title: Director, Business Intelligence
jobs.description:
**Overview**

AvePoint is seeking a Director, Business Intelligence to lead the global production BI operating model and turn governed enterprise data products into trusted, scalable reporting experiences. This role is accountable for how certified semantic models, Power BI solutions, controlled reporting, and production support are industrialized across the business - with clear standards for quality, release management, lifecycle ownership, and service delivery.

The Director, Business Intelligence will partner closely with Analytics and Data Engineering, which own business partnership, enterprise metric governance, Gold data products, advanced insights, and the underlying data platform. BI will consume those governed foundations and make them production-ready for leaders and teams across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, Product, People, and Operations. The ideal leader combines strong technical BI judgment with disciplined people management, global delivery leadership, and the ability to build a high-leverage operating model that scales through standards, reusable models, domain alignment, and AI-ready consumption.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Own the global BI strategy, operating model, service catalog, roadmap, and delivery standards for production reporting and semantic model deployment.

* Lead BI intake, prioritization, assignment, capacity planning, and delivery coordination; group demand into business themes and provide transparent status, dependencies, and business value to Analytics and executive stakeholders.

* Establish clear handoff criteria from Analytics prototypes and governed data products into BI production, including certification, QA, documentation, regression testing, release management, support, and retirement.

* Own production Power BI and semantic model engineering standards, including model performance, Direct Lake patterns, security, RLS, refresh reliability, QA, release controls, monitoring, SOX/controlled reporting requirements, and production support.

* Partner with Analytics to consume approved enterprise metrics and Gold data products without recreating or redefining business logic inside reports; escalate gaps in definitions, lineage, source quality, or data contracts.

* Build a domain-aligned BI delivery model across priority AvePoint 360 domains, with dedicated or clearly aligned BI engineering capacity for Customer/Sales/Partner, Commercial Growth, Product, and People data products as demand matures.

* Design and lead a global resourcing model that effectively uses existing teams and locations, including shared delivery partnerships, follow-the-sun support, and selective hiring where additional capacity or business proximity is required.

* Develop BI engineers and emerging leaders through coaching, technical standards, clear ownership, and rotational domain assignments that broaden business context while reducing key-person dependency.

* Drive report and semantic model rationalization by maintaining production inventory, eliminating duplicate logic, retiring legacy assets after validated migration, improving reuse, and tracking operating measures such as ownership clarity, incidents, cycle time, adoption, and recovered Analytics capacity.

* Partner with Analytics on AI and self-service readiness by ensuring production semantic models, metadata, security, documentation, and reporting outputs are trustworthy and reusable by both people and Data Agents.

  

**Qualifications:**

* Significant experience leading Business Intelligence, enterprise reporting, semantic modeling, analytics engineering, or a closely related function in a complex organization.

* Proven people leadership experience managing and developing technical BI teams; experience leading across regions, time zones, or distributed delivery models strongly preferred.

* Deep expertise with Microsoft Power BI and modern semantic model architecture; experience with Microsoft Fabric, Direct Lake, OneLake, deployment pipelines, AI-enabled analytics, or comparable cloud data platforms strongly preferred.

* Strong understanding of dimensional and semantic modeling, DAX, SQL, performance optimization, RLS/security, report architecture, governed self-service, and production support practices.

* Experience establishing BI engineering standards, QA and regression testing, CI/CD or release management, monitoring, documentation, and report lifecycle governance.

* Ability to distinguish enterprise metric governance and data-product ownership from BI production responsibilities, and to partner effectively with Analytics and Data Engineering without duplicating accountability.

* Demonstrated success managing intake, prioritization, workload balancing, stakeholder expectations, and a portfolio of production BI assets based on business value and capacity.

* Experience rationalizing legacy reports or semantic models and migrating users toward governed, reusable enterprise data products while maintaining business continuity.

* Experience with controlled or audit-sensitive reporting, including SOX-related processes, data quality controls, ownership documentation, or similar governance requirements preferred.

* Strong communication, technical judgment, and change-management skills, with the ability to review architecture, coach engineers, explain tradeoffs, lead through influence, and build durable partnerships across Analytics, Engineering, Finance, RevOps, Product, and other business functions.

  

**Benefits we offer:**

* Competitive market-based compensation

* Career progression and internal mobility opportunities across our global footprint in North America, EMEA, and APAC

* Unlimited PTO

The Salary Range for this role is $150,000 - $200,000. At AvePoint, we strive to offer competitive, fair, and equitable total rewards. The listed salary reference represents a market midpoint for initial planning, with final offers based on location, experience, skills, and qualifications.

**Board-Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) needed in Brooklyn & Staten Island.**  
**Full time school position!**

**SUMMARY**  
Under general supervision, the Board-Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) is responsible for conducting behavioral assessments, developing individualized treatment plans, and providing evidence-based interventions for students with developmental disabilities and autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The BCBA collaborates closely with teaching staff, related service providers, and families to promote a positive, inclusive, and supportive learning environment.  
  
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**  
Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:  

* Conducts Functional Behavior Assessments (FBA) and develops Behavior Intervention Plans (BIPs) tailored to individual student needs.
* Analyzes psychological, educational, and adaptive behavior assessments to inform behavioral programming.
* Designs and oversees implementation of behavior support strategies and skill acquisition programs based on the principles of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA).
* Collaborates with teachers and classroom staff to model and support evidence-based behavior management techniques.
* Attends and participates in Individualized Education Program (IEP) meetings, case conferences, and other team meetings to review progress and make necessary plan modifications.
* Provides in-situ coaching, modeling, and training for instructional staff to ensure fidelity of behavior support plans.
* Collects and analyzes data to monitor student progress and modifies programming as needed.
* Communicates effectively with parents/guardians regarding behavioral progress and strategies for home consistency.
* Provides staff development and training on behavior management, data collection, and implementation of ABA strategies.
* Supports classroom needs, including transitions, feeding, toileting, and crisis management, as necessary.
* Maintains accurate documentation in compliance with company policies, DOE regulations, and best practices in the field.
* Stays current with best practices and emerging research in behavior analysis and early childhood development.
* Performs other related duties as assigned by the Program Director.

**QUALIFICATIONS**  

* Master's degree in Applied Behavior Analysis, Psychology, Special Education, or related field.
* Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) certification in good standing.
* Minimum of 5 years of experience developing and implementing behavior support plans, preferably with preschool-aged children with developmental disabilities and/or autism.
* In-depth knowledge of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) principles and methodologies.
* Experience working in interdisciplinary team settings and school-based environments.
* Strong analytical, organizational, and time management skills.
* Effective communication skills, both verbal and written.
* Ability to coach, train, and support educators and paraprofessionals.
* Commitment to inclusive practices and cultural competence.
* Primary work takes place in a preschool setting with exposure to young children with varying needs.

Our purpose – Opening up a world of opportunity – explains why we exist. Here at HSBC, we use our unique expertise, capabilities, breadth, and perspectives to open up new kinds of opportunity for our more than 40 million customers. HSBC Americas is engaged in business in credit derivatives, emerging market and emerging market derivatives, mortgage, equity derivatives, fixed-income and interest rate derivatives, FX (Foreign Exchange), and commodities etc. Extensive risk models have been developed and well-documented to support these business activities. With Regulatory Stress Tests, methodology development and implementation, trading activities/strategies and risk management are more than ever driven by risk weighted return in the form of capital requirements, or risk weighted assets. At the meantime, risk engines are constantly being enhanced/consolidated to accommodate new regulations and anticipated changes. The mandate Risk Quantitative Analyst is to join the Global Risk Analytics team to research, develop and enhance traded risk methodologies, provide methodology support to regulatory stress test, businesses, traded risk management and control functions, interacting with regulatory agencies, and maintain and update the traded risk methodology documentation.

As Our Vice President Global Risk Analytics You Will

Review, validate and document risk methodologies across asset classes
Work on model assessment, monitoring tests, model performance and review and model risk governance. Responsible for conducting monthly model performance and review, investigating potential model performance issues and identifying areas for model enhancement
Manage the counterparty credit risk exposure for capital, limit and CVA (Credit Valuation Adjustment) calculation. According to regulatory standards to identify weaknesses and propose enhancements to satisfy all regulatory requirements and regulatory stress test)
Perform ad-hoc analysis in various aspects of risk measurements, stress tests, what-if analysis on the existing portfolios and during new product/transaction approval; and on demand quantitative support for businesses, and traded risk management and control functions
Work with the team to: develop advanced risk methodologies including sophisticated quantitative methodologies to measure counterparty credit and market risk exposures, and to enhance Value-at-Risk model, etc. Research and develop new risk methodologies to satisfy requirements of BASEL 3 and other regulatory frameworks. Research and develop methodology to address regulatory concerns and toward audit points removal

You´ll likely have the following qualifications to succeed in this role:

In depth knowledge on products and transactions in the various asset classes with solid understanding to their credit and market risk exposures and advanced quantitative methodologies to model and measure these risks. Strong working experience in quantitative financial methodologies (derivatives theory and models, probability theory, Mathematics, etc.) is required
Expertise in risk modeling development/enhancement. Demonstrated ability and experience in Regulatory Stress test, CVA, counteryparty credit risk and market risk models, and regulatory capital calculation
Excellent verbal and written skills. Must be able to explain and articulate complex quantitative and/or technical matters clearly, accurately and simply. Organized, detail-oriented and self-motivated, work independently, adhere to tight deadlines and develop and maintain healthy relationships with all internal clients and regulators

-

About Us

Orwashers Bakery (Orwashers.com) is a New York City institution, founded in 1916 in a small storefront on the Upper East Side. Today, Orwashers continues to be known for its New York classics including rye bread, pumpernickel, bagels, rugelach, black and white cookies and so much more.

In addition to selling bread to many of New York's top restaurants and gourmet grocery stores, Orwashers currently operates three retail bakeries in Manhattan and Long Island. We also deliver our breads and baked goods throughout Manhattan and distribute to carefully selected partners nationwide. While the company has grown since its humble beginnings over a century ago, the same values remain baked in: handmade classic breads and baked goods made fresh, locally, and with love each day.

What You Will Do

As FP&A Analyst, you will join the Finance & Accounting team and report directly to the CFO/COO. You will work across both the retail and wholesale sides of the business, partnering with Sales, Operations, and Accounting to turn the numbers into decision-making tools. Your analysis will show leadership where the margin is, which accounts are profitable, and what happens when commodity prices, wages, or the customer mix change.

Responsibilities:
Evaluate pricing and margins across products, channels, and customers, and recommend changes with their impact quantified.
Analyze ingredient, packaging, labor, and yield costs to identify variances and savings, and track whether those savings are realized.
Build and maintain a P&L by wholesale customer, and work with Sales to restructure accounts through pricing, delivery terms, minimums, or product mix.
Support the annual budget and rolling forecasts, and maintain financial models that run scenarios such as new or lost accounts, new locations, and commodity price swings.
Own weekly flash reporting and support month-end close reporting, including variance commentary, KPIs, and dashboards for leadership.
Handle some general accounting work (roughly 10–15% of the role) and support the CFO/COO on special projects and decisions.

Who You Are

You are a positive, solution-oriented team player whose curiosity and love of numbers help drive business improvements. You’re comfortable digging through messy data from accounting, POS, and inventory systems and making sense of it, and you can explain what the numbers mean to colleagues in Sales and Operations. You’re detail-oriented, work well independently, and enjoy the range that comes with a small finance team.

Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field
2 to 5 years in FP&A, financial analysis, or a similar role
Advanced Excel skills, including financial modeling
Experience in retail, food and beverage, CPG, or manufacturing
Nice to have: Experience with product or customer profitability analysis, commodity-driven cost structures, BI tools (Power BI, Tableau), and ERP/accounting systems (NetSuite, QuickBooks, etc.)

Benefits

Base salary: $95,000-$105,000
Annual performance-based bonus
Health insurance (company covers 70% for employee)
Long-term and short-term disability
401(k) with 4% company match (eligible after one year)
9 paid holidays plus 2 weeks PTO

The Lateral Conflicts Analyst is responsible for running and analyzing conflicts searches in support of the Firm’s lateral hiring process. The role includes researching corporate information from external sources, searching the Firm’s internal proprietary databases, and compiling and analyzing conflicts results for lateral candidates, highlighting critical issues for review by Conflicts Attorneys.

The Lateral Conflicts Analyst will work closely with Conflicts Attorneys, Resolution Analysts, other Conflicts Analysts, Lateral Partner Recruitment & Integration, Attorney Recruiting, and other members of the New Business Intake and Conflicts Departments. Because lateral clearance work involves candidate information that is highly confidential, the Analyst must exercise discretion at all times regarding candidate identities and the fact of a candidate’s interest in the Firm.

This position reports to the Sr. Manager, Intake/Conflicts.

Responsibilities Include

Reviewing lateral candidate submissions and matter lists to ensure clarity and completeness, and following up with the candidate and/or recruiting personnel where disclosures are incomplete or ambiguous.
Conducting conflicts searches on lateral candidates against the Firm’s conflicts database and other internal and external resources.
Performing data entry, searching, and analysis of conflicts data in the Firm’s conflicts and new matter intake systems in accordance with Firm policies and procedures.
Conducting research via external sources to establish corporate structures, affiliate relationships, and management profiles for parties appearing on candidate matter lists.
Compiling and preparing conflicts reports for review by Conflicts Attorneys, identifying and flagging potential actual, imputed, and positional conflicts for attorney assessment.
Verifying that all conflicts reports are complete, consistent, and accurate, and adhere to established standards and procedures for all conflicts of interest searches performed Firm-wide.
Supporting the implementation and maintenance of ethical screens for incoming lateral attorneys, including preparing supporting documentation and tracking certifications.
Maintaining accurate records of clearance searches, analysis, and related communications in support of the Firm’s audit-ready documentation standards.
Ensuring the timely and efficient processing of lateral clearance requests, including during periods of elevated recruiting activity.
Escalating complex, novel, or time-sensitive issues promptly to Conflicts Attorneys.
Contributing to process, procedure, and technology improvements to provide optimum customer service and efficiency.

Exceptional critical thinking and analytical skills, with a strong focus on accuracy, attention to detail, and consistency.

Excellent decision-making skills and a demonstrated ability to think on your feet.
Excellent people skills, with the ability to work in a team-oriented and collaborative environment.
Excellent customer service skills and proficiencies.
Comfortable working with attorneys and other legal staff.
Comfortable in a high-demand, fast-paced environment.
Ability to accept direction and constructive feedback.
Ability to take ownership and work independently to resolve issues, and sound judgment about when to escalate.
Ability to communicate clearly and effectively, both orally and in writing.
Discretion in handling confidential and sensitive information, including lateral candidate identities and prior client information.
Ability to work overtime as necessary.

Global Risk Management (GRM) leads bank-wide initiatives for management of all aspects of risk, including strategic, market, credit, compliance, liquidity, operational, model and reputational risk matters to support sustainable, profitable corporate growth.

In a data driven economy, strategic data asset management is foundational to add to the enterprise value. Within GRM, we have established the Data Strategy & Management (DSM) function. A key pillar of this function is a strong data management, data architecture and data platforms foundation.

Under the GRM DSM Executive’s leadership, the Quantitative Finance Analyst will help design features to simplify and optimize the data environment through data centric AI, and be accountable for contributing to the architecture & prototyping along with core algorithms for various data and AI powered solutions. Additionally, the analyst will also help evaluate data & AI tools and conduct proof of concepts & pilot projects to arrive at recommended solutions and develop remediation plans to implement those solutions.

Responsibilities:

Demonstrates knowledge of data & AI solutions, data platforms, context engineering, agentic AI workflows, data management & model governance practices and standards.
Define target-state architectures and design artifacts (data models, API specifications, integration patterns) for data platforms, reporting systems and governance workflows across risk domains.
Prototype UI/UX execution for data centric AI solutions by specifying user interfaces, approval flows, and response formats, guiding Figma design and Angular for stakeholder validation.
Design forward-deployed AI solutions (FDE model) by working closely with business stakeholders to rapidly prototype, customize, and productionize GenAI/LLM use cases (e.g., RAG, agentic workflows, risk analytics copilots).
Assist quantitative modelers by building data pipelines, API services for prototyping data & AI products using python, Spark, SQL, Relational, NoSQL and Graph data stores. Assist with prompt engineering, AI skills design and maintenance.
Operationalize governance by solutioning Semantic Data Intelligence agents for data contracts, lineage traceability, quality controls and monitoring; measure maturity and drive remediation programs for GRM information capabilities.
Evangelize and design new data & AI solutions and capabilities to support risk lines of businesses.
Participates in efforts to define the mission, goals, critical success factors, principles, and procedures for data strategy and information architecture.
Understands the end-to-end change impact by managing linkages from information capabilities to technical assets (operational + analytical)
