The ideal candidate for the current vacancy will possess one or more of the following characteristics:



A strong passion for environmental protection and creek stewardship
Knowledge of water quality parameters, watershed processes, best practices for storm water pollution prevention, and environmental regulations
Experience enforcing or maintaining compliance with environmental regulations
Experience collecting, analyzing, and presenting data in various formats 
Experience and enthusiasm developing and delivering environmental outreach or education campaigns to the public
Proven skills working independently and as a member of a collaborative team
Excellent verbal and written communication skills  


Please Complete a Thoughtful, Thorough Supplemental Questionnaire Submission
As part of the selection process, your responses to these questions will be scored using criteria specific to this position. Incomplete responses, or responses such as "See Resume", may not be considered.

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
At the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California, we deliver reliable water to a region with 19 million people—and to accomplish this, we rely on a team of talented employees: innovators, problem-solvers, and collaborators who make it all possible.

There is currently one (1) opening for Senior Environmental Specialist located at Union Station, Los Angeles, CA.

This recruitment may result in an eligibility list*.

Job Summary

The Senior Environmental Specialist leads the development, coordination, and implementation of complex environmental, health, and safety (EHS) compliance programs and technical studies across multiple Metropolitan sites. Serving as a technical subject matter expert, this role provides high-level program management and regulatory oversight across key disciplines including air quality, wastewater, stormwater, underground and aboveground storage tanks, hazardous materials and waste management, and health and safety. Based at the Los Angeles Headquarters, this position requires periodic travel and occasional overnight stays at field facilities throughout Southern California.

What You’ll Do



 Program & Compliance Leadership: Formulate compliance strategies, secure environmental permits, and review changing legislation to assess organizational impacts. Monitor federal, state, and local regulations to minimize risk for employees, the environment, and the public.  Technical Systems & Data Tracking: Utilize specialized Environmental Management Information System (EMIS) software and online platforms—including, but not limited to: SCAQMD Permit Database, CARB DOORS/R3 databases, CERS, GeoTracker, LACPW EPIC system, CalOES Spill Reporting, and the DTSC Hazardous WasteTracking System—to manage compliance data and streamline cloud-based tracking tools.  Agency Collaboration & Liaison: Serve as a primary point of contact for regulatory agencies, local governments, and member agencies. Lead negotiations, respond to inquiries, and establish strong partnerships with internal and external entities to represent Metropolitan's operational interests.  Internal Partnership & Training: Partner with internal teams to evaluate day-to-day compliance, deliver technical expertise, make recommendations to supervisors, and design EHS awareness and training programs for personnel.  Reporting & Documentation: Conduct staff analyses, execute complex environmental studies, and prepare technical reports, general correspondence, and Board letters for management review. 

Schedule: 9/80, Monday through Friday with every other Friday off

This job announcement has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work being performed by employees in this classification / job.

To view the full job description click here:  Sr. Environmental Specialist 

Schedule: 9/80 Start times are no earlier than 6 am and end times are no later than 6 pm.

Hybrid: Metropolitan’s current practice in this position is a hybrid work schedule. This typically includes two days a week in person and the other days remote. This is subject to change dependent on organizational needs. In addition, a telework policy is scheduled for negotiations and once completed and implemented, will provide final direction on the hybrid schedule.

EMPLOYMENT STANDARDS

Minimum Qualifications

Education and Experience: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in environmental science, engineering, biology, ecology, planning, or other directly related field, and eight years of progressively responsible experience, including two years at the Environmental Specialist level or equivalent; or a master’s degree from an accredited college or university in environmental science, engineering, biology, ecology, planning, or other directly related field, and six years of progressively responsible experience including two years at the Environmental Specialist level or equivalent.

Relevant/Related Experience is defined as: demonstrated experience serving as a lead for Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) programs, including managing multi-media environmental compliance areas such as Air Quality and Permitting, Underground Storage Tanks (UST), Industrial Wastewater, NPDES stormwater/wastewater reporting, and Hazardous Material Management.

Desirable Qualifications: 

 Environmental, Health, and Safety, Water Quality - Experience in public sector, water industry, public utilities; Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM); Certified Safety Professional (CSP); SCAQMD Certified Permitting Professional (CPP). 

Certifications, Licenses, And Registration Requirements

License(s): Valid California Class C Driver’s License or equivalent (required at time of application) that allows you to drive during your employment.

CLOSING

Benefits

 Competitive compensation  Excellent medical, dental, life, vision plans.  Deferred compensation in the form of a 401(k) plan (with matching contribution) and a 457 plan.  Retirement benefits under the California Public Employees' Retirement System  Tuition reimbursement  Training and advancement opportunities  Excellent working environment  Public transportation reimbursements  Hub of public transportation: rail, subway, buses, and taxis  On-site fitness center

jobs.description:
About Us

TRC, Member of WSP, is a global consulting environmental and engineering firm and one of the top design firms in the energy sector. Together, TRC and WSP’s 83,000 experts create positive, long-lasting impacts for our communities and our clients in the power and energy, transportation and infrastructure, environmental, and property and buildings sectors. As part of our team, you’ll discover a world of opportunities to connect with innovative thinkers, forge your path, and have fun tackling the world’s most challenging projects. At TRC, Member of WSP, you can have a rewarding career on every level.

TRC has long set the bar for clients who require more than just engineering, combining science with the latest technology to devise innovative solutions that stand the test of time. From pipelines to power plants, roadways to reservoirs, schoolyards to security solutions, clients look to TRC for breakthrough thinking backed by the innovative follow-through of an industry leader.

We recognize that the expertise of our staff is our strongest asset, so we generously reward employees for successful performance and invest in their careers through training and the development of new skills and certifications.

Overview

TRC's Strategic Health Sciences team is part of the Environmental Health, Safety, and Sustainability (EHS) practice within TRC and is a leader in toxicology, exposure science, and risk assessment.

The team is led by Dr. Dennis Paustenbach, a board-certified toxicologist and industrial hygienist with nearly 40 years of experience in risk assessment, environmental engineering, toxicology and occupational health. Dr. Paustenbach and his team provide expert witness testimony and analysis of the health effects of chemicals in sediments, air, soil, consumer products, foods, groundwater, and the workplace.

We are seeking a Principal Toxicologist who wishes to use scholarly approaches to answer complex exposure and health risk-related questions. Our vision is to engage with the most intellectually curious scientists to provide data-driven solutions to our clients. We approach each project in a collaborative, fast-paced environment to meet client needs. We are committed to maintaining an environment in which all of our team members feel respected and empowered to succeed.

Our multidisciplinary expertise includes engineering, exposure science, industrial hygiene, toxicology, applied risk assessment, risk communication, regulatory engagement, and supply chain and product stewardship. Most projects encompass exposures to chemicals in the workplace, community, or via consumer products. There is a heavy emphasis on reading and writing in this position, and candidates who apply should have proficient writing skills for technical and lay audiences, as well as a desire to work in a writing-intensive environment.

Critically evaluate published scientific papers and reports in the environmental sciences, industrial hygiene, toxicology, epidemiology, and occupational medicine fieldsPerform qualitative and quantitative exposure and risk assessments for a variety of chemicalsServe as a testifying expert in toxic tort litigationEvaluate and retain information from legal documents, including deposition and trial testimonyLead the production of technical work products, presentations, and proposalsInteract with clients on projects, both in-person and electronicallyConduct research that may be presented at scientific conferences or submitted to scientific journalsCandidate needs a high level of self-initiative

Our Mission

We understand our clients’ goals, and embrace them as our own, applying creativity, experience, integrity and dedication to deliver superior solutions to the world’s energy, environment and infrastructure challenges.

We will solve the challenges of making the Earth a better place to live — community by community.

GENERAL DESCRIPTION: 


The Division of Criminal Investigation, under the Attorney General's Office, seeks qualified applicants for the Forensic Specialist position in the Toxicology Unit. This family of positions includes those responsible for handling the physical evidence of a crime in a laboratory setting for agencies of the State of Wyoming. **Location: Irvine, CA \| Hybrid Field \& Office Role**

Make an Impact on Environmental Compliance \& Sustainability

Are you passionate about protecting the environment and helping organizations stay compliant with environmental regulations? We are seeking an Environmental Scientist to join a growing team supporting environmental compliance programs across a variety of industries.

This is an excellent opportunity for an early\-career environmental professional who enjoys a mix of office and field work, values professional growth, and wants exposure to a wide range of environmental regulations and compliance programs. You'll work alongside experienced environmental professionals, interact with clients, and gain hands\-on experience conducting compliance audits, inspections, sampling, and technical reporting.

**Work Schedule:** Approximately 50% office and 50% field work, including travel to client facilities throughout California and other locations as needed.

What You'll Do

* Conduct environmental compliance audits, inspections, and site assessments.
* Support hazardous waste, regulated waste, RCRA, stormwater, air quality, and related environmental compliance programs.

* Prepare technical reports, regulatory documentation, and compliance deliverables.
* Research environmental regulations and apply findings to client projects.

* Manage multiple assignments while meeting project schedules and deadlines.

What We're Looking For

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Geology, Biology, Chemistry, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline.
* 3\+ years of environmental compliance experience.
* Knowledge of RCRA, hazardous waste management, regulated waste, and environmental compliance regulations.
* Experience with stormwater, air quality, storage tanks, or other multimedia environmental programs.
* Strong technical writing and communication skills.
* Excellent organizational and time\-management abilities.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, and SharePoint.
* Ability to work independently and as part of a project team.

Why Apply?

* Diverse and challenging environmental projects.

**Education**

**Experience:**

* Project or task management with an emphasis on delivery

As a multicultural organization, we encourage individual achievement and recognize the strength of a diverse workforce. GHD is an equal opportunity employer. Company Description

Elkhorn Environmental Solutions, Inc. (Elkhorn) is a California-based environmental consulting firm providing strategic, technically sound solutions for environmental due diligence, site investigation, remediation, redevelopment, and regulatory closure. Our multidisciplinary team brings expertise in environmental engineering, geology, toxicology, risk assessment, and applied environmental science to help clients navigate complex environmental challenges and move projects forward.
We partner with property owners, developers, attorneys, lenders, businesses, regulatory agencies, and multidisciplinary project teams to develop practical strategies tailored to project goals, regulatory requirements, and site-specific conditions. Our work includes environmental due diligence and liability evaluation; soil, soil vapor, and groundwater investigation; vapor intrusion assessment; remediation design and optimization; redevelopment support; environmental risk assessment; and regulatory closure.

At Elkhorn, our focus extends beyond identifying environmental challenges, we develop clear, defensible pathways for addressing them. We deliver practical, technically sound strategies that help clients manage risk, navigate regulatory requirements, and move sites toward successful redevelopment and closure.

Role Description

This is a full-time opportunity based Northern California, with positions available in the San Francisco Bay Area, Sacramento Region, and Sierra Foothills for Environmental Scientists, Engineers, Geologists, and Business Support Professionals at all experience levels
. Technical professionals will support projects involving site assessments, soil, soil vapor, and groundwater investigations, remediation planning and implementation, and environmental due diligence. Day-to-day responsibilities may include conducting field work, collecting and managing environmental data, preparing technical reports and figures, supporting conceptual site model development and risk evaluations, and coordinating with clients, regulators, and project partners.
Business support professionals will support the administrative, accounting, financial, and operational functions of the firm. Responsibilities may include project administration, proposal and contract support, accounts payable and receivable, invoicing and billing support, expense tracking, financial recordkeeping, project accounting, data management, scheduling, and other administrative and operational activities that help keep our projects and business running efficiently.

Experience in environmental consulting or professional services is a plus but is not required for all positions.

We welcome candidates at all experience levels who are interested in growing with a collaborative environmental consulting firm.

jobs.title: Drinking Water Sampling Personnel – Shasta-Trinity National Forest, California
jobs.description:
Project Overview

I-2-I Solutions is seeking qualified drinking-water sampling personnel to support potable-water sampling services at U.S. Forest Service administrative sites throughout the Shasta-Trinity National Forest in Northern California
.

The work covers 10 water-system sites
located along Highway 36, Highway 299W, Highway 3, Interstate 5, and Highway 89. The required services include collection, storage, and transportation of drinking-water samples in accordance with applicable State and Federal requirements and the site-specific Bacteriological Sample Siting Plans (BSSPs).

Required Qualifications

Sampling personnel must be properly trained and qualified
to collect drinking-water samples.

Samplers must have either:

A minimum current California Level 1 Distribution System Operator certification, and/or
Specialized drinking-water sampling experience and education sufficient to qualify the individual as a properly trained and qualified sampler

Sampling Responsibilities

Responsibilities include:

Collecting routine drinking-water samples for Total Coliform and E. coli Presence/Absence testing
Collecting samples from the locations identified in the applicable BSSP
Measuring and documenting residual chlorine for bacteriological samples
Properly storing and transporting collected drinking-water samples
Following the approved laboratory's test-specific sample collection instructions
Following applicable State and Federal drinking-water sampling requirements
Collecting additional or repeat samples when directed and in accordance with the BSSP
Collecting optional chemical samples when required, except for Lead & Copper samples, which will be collected by Forest Service personnel

Routine Sampling Frequency

Routine bacteriological samples are to be collected within the first half of the applicable sampling month
.

Sampling frequency includes:

Yolla Bolla Corp Yard: one routine bacteriological sample monthly
Other Forest Service water systems identified for quarterly monitoring: one routine sample per quarter

Quarters are defined as:

1st Quarter: January-March
2nd Quarter: April-June
3rd Quarter: July-September
4th Quarter: October-December

Sampling Locations

Routine work is organized by the following routes:

Highway 36

Harrison Gulch Ranger Station / USFS Yolla Bolla Corp Yard

Highway 299W

Junction City Guard Station
Big Bar Ranger Station
Burnt Ranch Guard Station

Highway 3

Mule Creek Guard Station
Coffee Creek Guard Station

Interstate 5

Sims Guard Station
Lakeshore Guard Station
Turntable Bay Work Center

Highway 89

Ash Creek Guard Station

All sites located along the same sampling route are to be sampled during the same day
for routine sampling.

Site Coordination

When sampling requires access coordination with Forest Service personnel, advance coordination is required.

The project requires:

Coordination at least 48 hours in advance where access is needed
14-day notification prior to sampling visits, particularly where interior access, residences, barracks, or source sampling locations are involved

Site Issues During Sampling

If a sampling location is malfunctioning or inaccessible, sampling personnel may be required to:

Report malfunctioning sampling locations or water leaks
Provide a photograph and short description of the issue
Take a representative sample at another approved location shown on the site map when the designated sampling point is not usable

Repeat Sampling

Following a Total Coliform or E. coli Present
result, repeat sampling may be required.

Sampling personnel must be able to:

Take or accept repeat samples within 24 hours of laboratory notification of a Present result
Coordinate repeat sampling with the designated project point of contact
Collect repeat samples according to the applicable BSSP
Perform the required repeat set unless additional sampling is specifically directed

The BSSPs identify the specific routine, upstream, downstream, and source locations to be used for repeat sampling.

Project Period

The project includes:

Base Year: October 1, 2026-December 31, 2026
Option Year 1: January 1, 2027-December 31, 2027
Option Year 2: January 1, 2028-December 31, 2028

Important Note

Lead & Copper sample collection is not part of this sampling role.
Those samples will be collected by Forest Service personnel.

jobs.title: Water Agency Senior Environmental Specialist - Tribal Liaison
jobs.description:
Position Information

The Sonoma County Water Agency (Sonoma Water) seeks a Water Agency Senior Environmental Specialist to join our team as a Tribal Liaison!

Starting salary up to $67.07 /hour ( $139,983 /year) and a competitive total compensation package!*

Duties

Sonoma Water is seeking a Water Agency Senior Environmental Specialist to serve as the Agency's Tribal Liaison. This position will be responsible for establishing and fostering positive and constructive relationships with Tribes regarding Sonoma Water's water supply, flood control, sanitation, climate adaptation, and regional watershed management activities in the Russian River watershed. In this liaison role, you will work to build trust, enhance understanding, and support advancement of these activities. Other duties of this position include:

Preparing and reviewing documents in compliance with state, federal, and local environmental laws and regulations; land use planning projects; grant applications; and right-of-way activities
Planning and reviewing work related to evaluation and consideration of cultural and tribal resources
Communicating and delivering project information to Tribal representatives and governments as needed to engage Tribal participation or consultation on Sonoma Water projects and initiatives
Coordinating with Tribal representatives and governments in their review of Sonoma Water projects and environmental documents to facilitate receipt of and responses to Tribal comments
Managing agreements with consultant archeologists and drafting and managing Tribal monitoring agreements
Attending meetings (in the office, virtual, or in the field) with staff and managers from other Sonoma Water divisions
Regularly updating and working with the Environmental Resources Division Manager and Executive Team to develop and implement strategic positions supporting tribal consultations

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess Experience In Natural Resources, Water Resources Planning, And/or Community Liaison Experience, And Many Of The Following

Experience negotiating with Tribal communities and governments, regulatory agencies, and other project stakeholders
Excellent understanding and in-depth knowledge of Native American culture, history, tradition, perspectives and experiences
An understanding of tribal communities and governance in the Russian River watershed and/or San Francisco Bay region
Demonstrated knowledge of government-to-government sovereignty protocols
Demonstrated knowledge of AB 52 and the CEQA environmental review process for Tribal stakeholders
Strong stakeholder relationships with Native American Tribal governments and Tribal communities, demonstrated experience with Tribes, and knowledge and experience with industry best practices.
Experience organizing and facilitating public and stakeholder meetings, responding to concerns and issues from stakeholders, and gaining consensus on projects

Note: This position typically works Monday-Friday during regular business hours but may be required to work evening or weekend shifts to attend public meetings and community events. Work includes in-office (in-person) meetings, video conferencing (telework), travel to regional meetings, conferences and visits to project sites in terrestrial and aquatic environments during variable (sometimes inclement) weather conditions.

About Sonoma Water

Sonoma Water is a special district formed by the California State Legislature in 1949 and is responsible for providing a safe and reliable water supply to its customers in Sonoma and Marin counties. Sonoma Water also maintains 75 miles of flood control channels and provides sanitation services. Employing approximately 250 employees, Sonoma Water consists of four divisions, including Engineering & Resource Planning, Environmental Resources, Business Services & External Affairs, and Water/Wastewater Operations & Maintenance. Sonoma Water supports the concept of environmental sustainability, focusing on renewable power sources, and strives to be a leader in its water use efficiency and fishery restoration programs.

Employees of Sonoma Water are employees of a special district and are not subject to the provisions of the Civil Service Ordinance of the County of Sonoma.

What We Offer

Working at the County of Sonoma offers expansive opportunities for growth and development, the ability to be a part of a challenging and rewarding work environment, and the satisfaction of knowing you're working to better our communities. You can also look forward to flexible work arrangements and excellent benefits* including:

Hybrid Telework - A schedule that meets the needs of our staff, department operations, and the communities we serve may be available depending on the assignment
Salary Advancement - A salary increase after 1,040 hours (6 months when working full-time) for good work performance; eligibility for a salary increase for good performance every year thereafter, until reaching the top of the salary range
Paid Time Off - Competitive vacation and sick leave accruals, 12 paid holidays, and an additional 8 floating holiday hours per year
County Paid Health Premium Contributions - 100% premium contribution for the majority of employee-only and employee + family health plan options
Post-Retirement Health Reimbursement Arrangement - County contributions to help fund post-retirement health insurance/benefits
Retirement - A pension fully integrated with Social Security
Paid Parental Leave - May be eligible for up to 8 weeks (320 hours) after 12 months of County employment
Additional Benefits - Excellent dental, vision, disability, life insurance, employee assistance program, professional development, and more
Student Loan Debt Relief - County employees may be eligible for Public Service Loan Forgiveness through the U.S. Department of Education
Salary is negotiable within the established range. Benefits described herein do not represent a contract and may be changed without notice. Additional information can be found in the Service Employees International Union Local 1021 Memorandum Of Understanding (SEIU MOU) and our Employee Benefits Directory .

Sonoma Water is currently recruiting to fill a Water Agency Senior Environmental Specialist - Tribal Liaison position. This employment list may also be used to fill future full-time, part-time, or extra-help (temporary) positions as they occur during the active status of the list. Qualified County employees who wish to be considered for future positions should consider applying to this recruitment.
The formal title for this classification is Water Agency Senior Environmental Specialist.

Application submissions require the Supplemental Questionnaire be completed.

Minimum Qualifications

Experience & Education:
Any combination of education, training, and experience which would likely provide the required knowledge and abilities listed. Normally, this would include a Bachelor's degree in planning, engineering, water related, physical, and/or biological sciences, environmental studies, environmental law, natural resource or watershed management, or a closely related field; and three years of experience with engineering, environmental impact assessments and permitting, including at least one year at the level of Water Agency Environmental Specialist II, or equivalent.

License:
Possession of a valid driver's license at the appropriate level, including special endorsements, as required by the State of California, may be required depending upon assignment to perform the essential job functions of the position. The position advertised on this announcement requires possession of a valid California Driver’s License.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Ability to:
analyze and design project reports and determine probable effect on environment; write effectively and to use good judgment in the assembling, evaluation, and use of information; prepare and present various reports on the effect of projects on the environment to advisory boards, commissions, and elected bodies; assist in planning, scheduling, and training of other employees; make mathematical calculations; analyze situations accurately and adopt an effective course of action; establish and maintain effective relationships with other staff members, staff of other agencies, organizations, and the general public; prepare and disseminate information to media and others; prepare a wide range of clear, concise and informative reports, correspondence and brochures; operate office equipment including computers and supporting word processing, spreadsheet, and database applications.

Specialized Assignments Require The Following

Fish and Wildlife

Working knowledge of:
fishery and wildlife management principles and methods; the classification, life histories, ecology, habitats, parasites, and diseases of fresh-water fish and California wildlife; research methodology; wildlife resource management, including watershed, range, forestry, fishery, wildlife and recreation techniques and equipment in making biological investigations of fish and wildlife; materials, equipment, and techniques used in fishery and wildlife habitat improvement; fishery considerations in the design, location, and construction of public works projects relating to streams, lakes, and ecological areas.

Botanical, Wetland Resource and Soil Morphology

vegetation and soil management principles and methods; the classification and morphology of soil, and botanical identification, classification, and life histories of plants; botanical soil research methodology; techniques and equipment in making botanical and soil investigations; materials, equipment, and techniques used in botanical habitat enhancements or soil structure improvements; botanical considerations in the design, location, and construction of public construction projects relating to wetlands, riparian areas and other ecological areas.

Arboricultural/Revegetation

Working knowledge of:
the classification and identification of native plants and ornamental trees; the growth habits, parasites, diseases, habitat, and life histories of native plants and ornamental trees; sources of native plants; soil amendments and fertilizers; irrigation methods, needs, and materials; erosion control methods and materials; planting monitoring and maintenance methods; tree management principles and methods; research methodologies; forestry, woodland and range resource management; techniques used in arboriculture; considerations needed to design, locate, and construct revegetation projects in urban and natural settings and to be compatible with the desired function of flood control, water supply, and sanitation facilities; arboricultural considerations in the design, location, and construction of public projects.

Environmental Analysis

Working knowledge of:
current standard methodologies for environmental impact analysis and report preparation; principles and methods of effective public outreach including preparation and filing of various environmental notices as required by law; environmental case law particul
